name: png-codec
prompt:
Build a fully functional PNG encoder and decoder from scratch in Python. No image libraries allowed — you are reimplementing the PNG specification (RFC 2083) by hand.

DECODER: PNG → raw pixel array

Chunk Parsing:
- Read and validate the PNG signature (\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n)
- Parse all chunk types: length, type, data, CRC
- Validate CRC-32 for every chunk — raise on mismatch
- Must handle chunk ordering rules per spec (IHDR first, IEND last, etc.)

Supported Chunk Types:
- IHDR — image header (width, height, bit depth, color type, compression, filter, interlace)
- IDAT — image data (may be split across multiple chunks — must concatenate before decompressing)
- PLTE — palette (required for color type 3)
- tEXt, zTXt, iTXt — text metadata (parse and expose)
- bKGD, gAMA, cHRM, sRGB — color metadata (parse and expose)
- tIME — timestamp
- IEND — end marker
- Unknown chunks — skip ancillary, error on critical

Decompression + Filtering:
- Decompress IDAT data using Python's zlib.decompress
- Implement all 5 PNG filter types per spec:
  * None (0)
  * Sub (1)
  * Up (2)
  * Average (3)
  * Paeth (4) — must implement Paeth predictor function exactly per spec
- Support all color types: 0 (Grayscale), 2 (RGB), 3 (Indexed/palette), 4 (Grayscale+Alpha), 6 (RGBA)
- Support bit depths: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16
- Support Adam7 interlacing (7-pass decode)

ENCODER: raw pixel array → PNG

Chunk Writing:
- Write valid PNG signature
- Write IHDR with correct fields
- Write PLTE if color type 3
- Write IDAT: compress with zlib.compress, split into chunks if data exceeds 8192 bytes
- Write IEND
- Compute and write correct CRC-32 for every chunk

Filtering:
- Implement all 5 filter types for encoding
- Implement adaptive filter selection: for each scanline, try all 5 filters and pick the one that minimizes the sum of absolute values of filtered bytes (per spec recommendation)

Supported Output:
- Color types: 0 (grayscale), 2 (RGB), 6 (RGBA)
- Bit depth: 8 and 16
- No interlacing required for encoder

CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENTS:

Decoder:
- Download and test against PNG test suite: http://www.schaik.com/pngsuite/ (covers all color types, bit depths, filter types, interlacing, corrupt files)
- For each valid image: compare every pixel value against PIL.Image.open() output — must be identical
- For each corrupt image in the suite: must raise an appropriate exception, not silently produce wrong output
- If any pixel mismatches, debug and fix

Encoder:
- Encode a raw pixel array → PNG file
- Decode that file with your own decoder → must get back identical pixel values (round-trip test)
- Also decode with Pillow → must be identical
- Test round-trip for: grayscale 8-bit, RGB 8-bit, RGBA 8-bit, RGB 16-bit
- Verify your encoded files pass pngcheck if available

Cross-validation:
- Decode a PNG with Pillow → encode with your encoder → decode with your decoder → compare against original Pillow output — must be pixel-perfect

PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS:
- Decode a 1920x1080 RGBA PNG in under 10 seconds (pure Python is slow, but correctness first)
- If slower, profile with cProfile and optimize the bottleneck (likely Paeth filter or pixel unpacking)
- Report decode time for 1920x1080 in README

CONSTRAINTS:
- No use of PIL, Pillow, cv2, imageio, pypng, or any image library anywhere in implementation
- zlib is allowed (it's in stdlib) — do not implement zlib from scratch
- struct for binary parsing is allowed
- Standard library only
- Pillow is allowed only in the test suite for ground-truth comparison

DELIVERABLES:
- png_decoder.py
- png_encoder.py
- tests.py — full test suite with Pillow comparison
- benchmark.py — decode time for large image
- README.md — architecture, Paeth implementation notes, benchmark results, known limitations
description: Tests ability to implement a complex binary format specification (PNG/RFC 2083) from scratch, including chunk parsing, CRC validation, filtering algorithms, compression, and cross-validation against reference implementations
